story.title: The Changemaker Trio Save the River
paragraphs_en: One day, Hali the elephant, Maya the bird, and Kenn the turtle were sitting around in the midday sun trying to figure out something to do. “Let’s go climb on the big rocks!” said Hali. “That’s too scary,” answered Kenn as he shrunk back into his shell, “Maybe we should take a nap instead.” “It’s too hot out to take a nap,” Maya remarked, “Let’s go for a swim!”

The Changemaker Trio all excitedly murmured their agreement and set off towards the river. When they arrived, a disgusting, strong smell greeted them and the surrounding bank was covered in garbage. “I don’t remember the river smelling this badly,” Hali observed, “It’s quite strange.” “Is it safe?” Kenn wondered out loud, “I don’t want to get sick.” “Of course it’s safe,” Maya responded as she waded in, “we have always swum here.” “I’m going to stay out here and just watch you guys,” Kenn announced.

Hesitantly, Hali followed Maya into the cloudy, smelly water. The two began to play a fun game of tag. Hali began to squirt the water up into the air using her trunk. Hali and Maya laughed and splashed as they cooled off from the heat. “Are you sure you don’t want to come in?” Maya asked Kenn. “I’m sure. The river doesn’t look very nice today,” answered Kenn.

Maya dove gracefully underwater. She resurfaced coughing and had large dots all over her body. “I don’t feel so good,” Maya stated as she made her way out of the water, “I don’t feel very good at all.” Seconds later, Hali followed her out. “Now that I think about it, I don’t feel too well either,” Hali agreed, “My head really hurts and I have a rash.” “Oh no,” Kenn commented, “I knew it wasn’t safe. We should go to Doctor Darya.”

The three friends slowly began their trek across the forest and towards Doctor Darya’s office in the grassy land. Kenn led the way for the other two animals who were still far from feeling their best. As the Sun began to descend from the sky, the three animals finally approached the Doctor’s office. Knock! Knock! Knock! The animals stood as they waited to be welcomed into Doctor Darya’s care. Finally, a large rhinoceros approached the animals with a warm smile on her face. “Hello! I’m Doctor Darya,” the rhino said, “Come on in and tell me what’s wrong.”

The friends entered the office and proceeded to tell the story of what had brought them there. “It was so hot out and we wanted to go swimming in the river,” Maya described. “It stunk so bad and there was trash everywhere,” said Hali. “But they still went in,” Kenn added. “We probably shouldn’t have,” Hali noted, “It gave me a headache and a rash.” “It gave me a rash and a cough,” Maya related.

“You are probably right,” Doctor Darya remarked, “That river has become extremely polluted because of the human’s lack of sewage treatment. That means that when the humans go to the washroom, their waste isn’t always properly contained. This contaminates the water and brings a lot of big problems.” “That’s not good,” Hali said unhappily, “Can we help fix this?” “Yes, we need all the help we can get to help bring awareness to the pollution of water,” Doctor Darya offered. “Everyone can do their part in helping fix these issues whether you be a kid or an adult. You could help by telling people about the issues with wastewater treatment or you could even help by cleaning up the trash you saw on the bank.”

“That’s so cool that we can help,” Maya exclaimed, “I never knew that I could help make a difference even though I’m a kid. Let’s start helping as soon as possible!” As soon as Maya and Hali felt better, The Changemaker Trio returned to the dirty riverbank, this time, along with their other friends. They were ready to help make a difference by picking up the trash and posting posters describing the issue of wastewater treatment. Hali, Maya, and Kenn left feeling good that they now understood that they could make a difference despite their age. They want you to know that you can make a difference too!
